title: Patch: the browser tab says it is your move during the mulligan and when a prompt waits on you, not only on your turn
thread:
**Issue #1792 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1792: Patch: the browser tab says it is your move during the mulligan and when a prompt waits on you, not only on your turn
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
In an online match the browser tab's title reads "Your turn", so a player who switched tabs can find the game. Today it follows only whose turn it is:
- During the opening mulligan, the player going first sees "Your turn" the whole time, even after pressing Ready.
- The player going second, who still has to choose, sees nothing.
- A choice the game asks of you during your opponent's turn doesn't flag the tab either.

Once built, the tab is flagged exactly when the game is waiting on you.

## Why
- `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx:325-328`: `yourTurn = view !== null && view.result === null && view.active === view.viewer`.
- A new game's `active` is P1 (`crates/engine/src/state.rs:2119`) and stays P1 until the first turn starts (`turn.rs:383`), so P1 always reads as active during the mulligan.
- The view already carries the mulligan as `PlayerView.mulligan` (`youReady`, `opponentReady`; `wire/generated/MulliganView.ts`, R265, R266). The title never reads it.
- A prompt waiting on the viewer is `pending.forYou`. `promptHolderOf` (`match.tsx:66-70`) already works out who a prompt waits on, but the title doesn't use it.
- The co-op table has the same rule (`apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.tsx:153-161`, `view.own.active === view.own.viewer`).
- The only title test (`routes/match.test.tsx:558-568`) covers just the active-player case.

## Proposal
Add one small pure helper, `awaitsYou(view)`. It is true only when there is no result and:
- the mulligan is open and the viewer has not answered it (`!mulligan.youReady`); otherwise
- a prompt is open and it is the viewer's (`pending.forYou`); otherwise
- it is the viewer's turn (`active === viewer`).

Use it for the 1v1 title, and on `view.own` for the co-op title, keeping co-op's `round > 0` and ended-duel checks. It reads only the view (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, `apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx` and the co-op route's test
- §2.1 (the mulligan). No spec change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Mulligan open, viewer p2 not yet ready: the title is "Your turn · JackiOh".
- [ ] Mulligan open, viewer p1 already ready: the title is the match's plain title, even though `active` is p1.
- [ ] On the opponent's turn, a prompt with `forYou: true` flags the title.
- [ ] On the viewer's turn, a prompt waiting on the opponent does not flag it.
- [ ] The existing active-player test still passes, and the co-op route gets the same mulligan and prompt cases.
- [ ] The web test files touched, typecheck and eslint pass.

## Size and risks
Extra small: one helper, two call sites and a handful of tests. No risk to play: it changes only `document.title`.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40115854888)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

The browser tab reads "Your turn · JackiOh" exactly when the game waits on the viewer, in a 1v1 match and at the co-op table. Concretely:
- During the opening mulligan, a seat that still owes its answer is flagged and a seat that is ready is not, whatever `active` says.
- A prompt the viewer holds (`pending.forYou`) flags the tab on the opponent's turn.
- A prompt waiting on the other player keeps the tab plain even on the viewer's turn.
- With no prompt open, the viewer's own turn flags it, as today.
- A finished game is never flagged.

One pure helper, `awaitsYou`, decides this from the view alone (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Both routes use it, and each route gets tests.

## Files to touch

| File | Kind | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/game/net.ts` | change | New exported `awaitsYou(view, yourTurn?)`, in a new section before `// The dev handle` |
| `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx` | change | The title effect uses `awaitsYou(view)`; `yourTurn` is renamed `yourMove` |
| `apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.tsx` | change | `yourMove` uses `awaitsYou(view.own, …)`, with `round > 0` and the ended check applied to the turn only |
| `apps/web/src/net/head.ts` | change | The doc comment on `documentTitleFor` (it now says "while it is the player's turn") |
| `apps/web/src/game/net.test.ts` | change | New `describe("awaitsYou (#1792)")` |
| `apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx` | change | A `pushView` helper and three title tests |
| `apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.test.tsx` | change | New `describe` with two title tests |

Do not touch any crate, `spec/`, `BUILD.md`, `e2e/`, `apps/web/src/wire/`, `apps/web/src/test/fixtures.ts`, any `package.json` or config, or the i18n catalogs: no new string, since "Your turn" already exists.

What governs this:
- §2.1 step 3 and R265/R266, the concurrent mulligan. R266 says each seat's view shows its own prompt until it answers, then `pending: { forYou: false, pendingFor: <other> }`. `crates/engine/src/view_for.rs` `mulligan_pending_view` does exactly that.
- §13.2: co-op round 0 is the mulligans.
- §13.3: a seat that has ended its turn "still answers a prompt it holds".

No spec change, no ruling, no patch fragment (no card plays differently).

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/game/net.ts`: add the helper.** Insert this just above the line `// The dev handle (BUILD M5-T3, consumed by e2e/support/commands.ts)` (about line 849), with one blank line on each side:

   ```ts
   // What waits on the viewer (#1792)

   /**
    * #1792: whether the game waits on the viewer, for the tab's title. Never once the game is over;
    * while a prompt is open, only when it is the viewer's (`pending.forYou`), the mulligan's included
    * (R265, R266: a seat that has answered sees the other seat's as `forYou: false`); otherwise on
    * `yourTurn`, the viewer's own turn unless the caller says what its turn is (the co-op round, §13.3).
    */
   export function awaitsYou(view: PlayerView, yourTurn: boolean = view.active === view.viewer): boolean {
     if (view.result !== null) return false;
     if (view.pending !== null) return view.pending.forYou;
     return yourTurn;
   }
   ```

   `PlayerView` is already imported at the top of the file.

2. **`apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, the import.** Add `awaitsYou,` as the first name in the `import { installDevHandle, remainingMs, useMatch, viewDerivedState, … } from "../game/net.ts";` block.

3. **`apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, the title effect (lines 324–328).** Replace the comment and the `const yourTurn = …` line, and rename the variable in the effect:

   ```ts
     // #1792: the tab says when the game waits on the player (its mulligan, a prompt it holds, or its
     // turn: `awaitsYou`), so a match in a background tab can be found.
     const yourMove = view !== null && awaitsYou(view);
     useEffect(() => {
       document.title = yourMove ? `${t("Your turn")} · ${SITE_NAME}` : documentTitleFor(paths.match(matchId));
     }, [yourMove, matchId, locale]);
   ```

   Change nothing else in the file. `promptHolderOf` stays as it is.

4. **`apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.tsx`, the import.** Change it to `import { awaitsYou, installDevHandle, viewDerivedState } from "../game/net.ts";`.

5. **`apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.tsx`, `yourMove` (lines 152–158).** Replace the comment and the expression; the `useEffect` below it stays as it is:

   ```ts
     // #1792: the tab says when the game waits on the seat, so a match in a background tab is found: a
     // prompt it holds, its mulligan's included, even once it has ended its turn (§13.3); otherwise its
     // own turn, once the round is running (round 0 is the mulligans, §13.2) and until it ends it.
     const yourMove =
       view !== null &&
       view.result === null &&
       awaitsYou(view.own, view.round > 0 && view.own.active === view.own.viewer && view.team.ended[slot] !== true);
   ```

6. **`apps/web/src/net/head.ts`, the doc comment on `documentTitleFor` (lines 72–73).** Replace its two text lines with these three. Change nothing else.

   ```ts
    * The tab title for a path: "Sign in · JackiOh", and plain "JackiOh" on the landing page. The
    * match and co-op screens replace it with "Your turn · JackiOh" while the game waits on the player
    * (`awaitsYou`, game/net.ts).
   ```

7. **Write the tests below**, then run the commands in **Tests**.

```

  function open(): void {
    act(() => {
      latest().readyState = 1;
      latest().onopen?.({});
    });
  }

   | Pushed view | Expected title |
   | --- | --- |
   | `a1(3, {})` | `"Your turn · JackiOh"` |
   | `a1(3, { pending: { forYou: false, pendingFor: "p2" } })` | `"Duos · JackiOh"` |
   | `a1(3, { active: "p2", pending: flood })` | `"Your turn · JackiOh"` |
   | `a1(3, {}, [true, false])` | `"Duos · JackiOh"` |
   | `a1(3, { pending: flood }, [true, false])` | `"Your turn · JackiOh"` |

Without steps 3 and 5, each new route test fails on at least one assertion: the not-ready mulligan rows, the ready Player 1 row and the prompt rows.

Commands:
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/net.test.ts src/routes/match.test.tsx src/duos/DuosRoute.test.tsx` (its `pretest` builds the wasm first)
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/net.ts apps/web/src/game/net.test.ts apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx apps/web/src/routes/match.test.tsx apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.tsx apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.test.tsx apps/web/src/net/head.ts`

If a rendered board throws on a prompt with empty `options`, give it the one Flood option, as in the rows above. Do not change what the test asserts.

## Done when

- [ ] `awaitsYou` exists in `apps/web/src/game/net.ts` exactly as in step 1, and both routes use it (steps 3 and 5).
- [ ] 1v1: viewer p2 mulligan not ready → "Your turn · JackiOh"; viewer p1 ready with `active` p1 → "Match · JackiOh"; a `forYou` prompt on the opponent's turn flags it; the opponent's prompt on the viewer's turn does not.
- [ ] The existing "puts Your turn in the tab while it is the player's turn" test passes unchanged.
- [ ] Co-op: the mulligan and prompt cases above pass. Round 0 and the ended check still keep the turn alone from flagging.
- [ ] All three test files pass; web typecheck and eslint on the touched files are clean.
- [ ] The harness checks (rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests) are green. Nothing in `crates/` or `apps/web/src/wire/` changed, so they should be untouched.

## Risks

- **Hidden information and rule 7.** The helper reads only `PlayerView` fields the server already sends. No rule is enforced; it changes only `document.title`. Determinism and replay are untouched.
- **Co-op round 0.** Kept as a hard `&&` around the whole expression, `round > 0` would stop the co-op mulligan from ever flagging (round 0 is the mulligans, §13.2). It must sit inside the `yourTurn` argument only, as step 5 has it. The same goes for `team.ended[slot]`: per §13.3, a seat that has ended still answers its prompts.
- **jsdom keeps `document.title` between tests.** Each new test's first assertion follows a fresh mount, whose effect writes the title, so a stale title cannot make a test pass by accident.
- **Bundle.** The helper goes in `game/net.ts`, which both lazy routes already import, not in `routes/match.tsx`. Importing the match route into `DuosRoute.tsx` would pull its whole module graph into the co-op chunk.

## Open questions

None for a person. The planner settled these choices:
- **No separate mulligan clause.** The issue proposes checking `mulligan.youReady` before `pending`. Per R266 and `view_for.rs` `mulligan_pending_view`, the view's `pending` already is the viewer's own mulligan prompt (`forYou: true`) until it answers, and `{ forYou: false }` after. The clause can never change the answer for a view the server sends, and testing it would need views the engine never produces. Rejected: adding it anyway.
- **The co-op turn is an argument.** It is the optional `yourTurn` argument rather than a second helper or a co-op copy of the logic. Rejected: keeping `round > 0` and `ended` as outer conditions, which would break the co-op mulligan and the ended-seat prompt cases the issue asks for.
- **The helper lives in `game/net.ts`.** Rejected: `routes/match.tsx` beside `promptHolderOf` (the bundle reason in Risks) and `game/contract.ts` (neither route imports it).
````

## Goal

The browser tab reads "Your turn · JackiOh" exactly when the game waits on the viewer, in a 1v1 match and at the co-op table. Concretely:
- During the opening mulligan, a seat that still owes its answer is flagged and a seat that is ready is not, whatever `active` says.
- A prompt the viewer holds (`pending.forYou`) flags the tab on the opponent's turn.
- A prompt waiting on the other player keeps the tab plain even on the viewer's turn.
- With no prompt open, the viewer's own turn flags it, as today.
- A finished game is never flagged.

One pure helper, `awaitsYou`, decides this from the view alone (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Both routes use it, and each route gets tests.

| `apps/web/src/duos/DuosRoute.tsx` | change | `yourMove` uses `awaitsYou(view.own, …)`, with `round > 0` and the ended check applied to the turn only |

What governs this:
- §2.1 step 3 and R265/R266, the concurrent mulligan. R266 says each seat's view shows its own prompt until it answers, then `pending: { forYou: false, pendingFor: <other> }`. `crates/engine/src/view_for.rs` `mulligan_pending_view` does exactly that.
- §13.2: co-op round 0 is the mulligans.

   ```ts
   // What waits on the viewer (#1792)

   /**
    * #1792: whether the game waits on the viewer, for the tab's title. Never once the game is over;
    * while a prompt is open, only when it is the viewer's (`pending.forYou`), the mulligan's included
    * (R265, R266: a seat that has answered sees the other seat's as `forYou: false`); otherwise on
    * `yourTurn`, the viewer's own turn unless the caller says what its turn is (the co-op round, §13.3).
    */
   export function awaitsYou(view: PlayerView, yourTurn: boolean = view.active === view.viewer): boolean {
     if (view.result !== null) return false;
     if (view.pending !== null) return view.pending.forYou;
     return yourTurn;
   }
   ```

````markdown
# Plan (opus, strong)

## Goal

The browser tab reads "Your turn · JackiOh" exactly when the game waits on the viewer, in a 1v1 match and at the co-op table. Concretely:
- During the opening mulligan, a seat that still owes its answer is flagged and a seat that is ready is not, whatever `active` says.
- A prompt the viewer holds (`pending.forYou`) flags the tab on the opponent's turn.
- A prompt waiting on the other player keeps the tab plain even on the viewer's turn.
- With no prompt open, the viewer's own turn flags it, as today.
- A finished game is never flagged.

One pure helper, `awaitsYou`, decides this from the view alone (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Both routes use it, and each route gets tests.

   ```ts
   // What waits on the viewer (#1792)

   /**
    * #1792: whether the game waits on the viewer, for the tab's title. Never once the game is over;
    * while a prompt is open, only when it is the viewer's (`pending.forYou`), the mulligan's included
    * (R265, R266: a seat that has answered sees the other seat's as `forYou: false`); otherwise on
    * `yourTurn`, the viewer's own turn unless the caller says what its turn is (the co-op round, §13.3).
    */
   export function awaitsYou(view: PlayerView, yourTurn: boolean = view.active === view.viewer): boolean {
     if (view.result !== null) return false;
     if (view.pending !== null) return view.pending.forYou;
     return yourTurn;
   }
   ```
````
